issues.problem: admin_author is tagged selection:'match' and is listed in target_roles alongside the two genuine message matches, but admin_author/admin_membership are users/user_teams rows, not the referent table (messages). This violates the stated rule that target/candidate roles must name only the referent table; intermediate binding records belong in support roles. The design's own mechanical_design_errors field already flags this, confirming it is a real defect rather than a false positive.
issues.repair: Change roles.admin_author.selection to 'support' (matching admin_membership) and remove admin_author/admin_membership from obligations[0].target_roles, leaving only matching_message_engineering and matching_message_general as targets.

issues.problem: A brand-new message is introduced for the Robert Chen negative (id 1706069700.000002) even though the base seed already contains several real messages authored by U_ROBERT (e.g., 1706067472.000000, 1706068012.000000, 1706069328.000000) in channels the bot can see, making the fabricated addition unnecessary.
issues.repair: Reuse an existing U_ROBERT message (e.g., 1706067472.000000 in C_INFRA) as the member-role negative instead of inventing a new row.

rationale: The prompt asks for every message posted by the named admin 'Robert Walsh,' and the route MESSAGE->USER->WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP is meaningfully exercised: the admin claim in the prompt is verified via the same-record user_teams role, not merely assumed from the name, and the answer_attributes correctly surface both message content and the membership role pair. The two matched messages (1699824000.000987, 1700173200.000456) are the only messages authored by U03ROBERT23 in the seed, confirming completeness. Negatives are well-chosen and semantically grounded: Robert Chen shares the display name but has role='member' (name-collision test), Morgan Freeman is a true admin with no authored content (missing-relationship test), and both are real, non-fabricated seed users/relations. Channel membership data confirms the acting bot (U01AGENBOT9) is a member of every channel where Robert Walsh actually posted (C01ABCD1234, C03IJKL9012), so conversations.history + users.info gives real, non-hidden-ID discovery consistent with the domain's documented users.info/workspace-membership exposure. The only defects are mechanical role-labeling issues already self-flagged for compiler repair and a minor, non-blocking redundancy in the negative message construction; neither requires a prompt-level revision.
